definitions.explanation: The position or way in which someone holds their body.
One's way of thinking about or approaching something.

examples.japanese: {姿勢|しせい}を{正|ただ}して{座|すわ}ってください。
{猫背|ねこぜ}を{直|なお}して{良|よ}い{姿勢|しせい}を{保|たも}ちたい。
examples.english: I want to fix my hunched back and maintain good posture.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}に{対|たい}する{姿勢|しせい}が{評価|ひょうか}された。
examples.english: My attitude toward work was appreciated.

notes:
{姿勢|しせい} can refer to both physical posture and mental attitude/stance.

Common collocations:
- {姿勢|しせい}を{正|ただ}す (to straighten one's posture)
- {良|よ}い{姿勢|しせい} (good posture)
- {悪|わる}い{姿勢|しせい} (bad posture)
- 〜に{対|たい}する{姿勢|しせい} (attitude toward ~)
- {前向|まえむ}きな{姿勢|しせい} (positive attitude)
- {低|てい}{姿勢|しせい} (low profile, humble attitude)

For physical posture:
- {正|ただ}しい{姿勢|しせい} (correct posture)
- {姿勢|しせい}が{悪|わる}い (to have bad posture)

For attitude/stance:
- {積極的|せっきょくてき}な{姿勢|しせい} (proactive attitude)
- {消極的|しょうきょくてき}な{姿勢|しせい} (passive attitude)
